# ISSUE-311 preserved-candidate verification plan

Preserve the existing Linux harness-tools Bubblewrap runtime-closure implementation. Complete remaining focused verification and only minimal corrections demonstrated necessary by that verification. This is a fresh, human-gated plan, not a redesign or an approval.

## Binding, dimensions, and gate

- Candidate: `b3e19745c76ef89be1b131edb9a329e953dd6702`.
- Replaced predecessor: `ca3c72f5020b9378eae53863367be6538c927d95`.
- Operator reports the candidate merges current main28 cleanly. This snapshot has no Git metadata, so ancestry, exact candidate bytes and predecessor-to-candidate differences must be verified by the coordinator in its preserved checkout before evidence is attributed to this candidate. Do not substitute another revision silently.
- Approved dimensions/profile: small / known / sensitive; total claim budget 16 hours. The remaining verification/minimal-correction cycle fits that scope.
- Obtain fresh independent review and actual independent maintainer approval bound to current WorkUnit, trusted policy, PLAN.md and TEST_PLAN.md digests. The historical approval does not approve these new artifacts. This planner neither implements nor approves the human gate.
- Reconciliation is a separate, explicit operator action after actual human approval. This plan does not reconcile, replace authoritative state, stage, renew, validate or publish anything.

## What we know

- WORKUNIT.md requires deterministic Maven/Gradle-shaped launches and adversarial preservation of the restore boundary; installed-client checks belong to PR review. Harness changes are forbidden.
- The implementation already exists: `internal/sandbox/restore_runtime_linux.go:473` selects only fixed launcher spellings; `:556` stages snapshots; `:628` renders sorted individual read-only mounts and aliases. These are existing files, not proposed new files.
- `restore_runtime_linux.go:31,59,71,163,172` provides the private fixture seam, production ownership/permission checks, pinned traversal, identity revalidation and bounded reads. `:266` resolves typed JAR links and bounded enumeration. `:332` defines six exact public metadata pairs; `:337-338` includes both unlimited-policy targets. `:341` validates Java security properties; `:423` validates exact Java aliases and metadata.
- `internal/sandbox/restore_linux.go:43,66` integrates runtime flags in the existing restore launcher. Existing broad /usr/bin and /usr/lib mounts remain as before; added inputs must stay individual snapshots. `:23` retains finite resource flags. Helper-only GOMAXPROCS is already present at `:21`; this plan does not revisit helper startup or packaging.
- Existing tests cover layouts (`restore_runtime_linux_test.go:162`), metadata (`:218`), excluded defaults (`:288`), unsafe inputs (`:327`), snapshots (`:381`), limits (`:440,819`), ordinary-executor separation (`:491`), fixture launches (`:518`), integrity (`:739`), deduplication (`:772`) and policy races (`:884`). `changes/unreleased/311.md` already exists.
- The user reports the helper is now installed pure Go and the two Maven packages have been installed. Prior ca3c72 actual-host manifest proof passed and is available to the coordinator. These supersede stale prior-artifact statements that installation/proof remain undone; they are supplied evidence, not new measurements by this planner.
- `git rev-parse HEAD` fails in this snapshot. No tests or host probes were run during planning. Project/architecture/conventions and `.claude/commands/swarm-plan.md` were read; rg is unavailable, so source searches used grep.

## Preserved manifest and exclusions

Keep code-owned Maven `/usr/share/maven/bin/mvn`, exactly one immediate `boot/plexus-classworlds-*.jar`, immediate `lib/*.jar`, and generated `bin/m2.conf` with existing `runtimeClassworlds` bytes. Keep Gradle `/usr/share/gradle/bin/gradle`, required `lib/gradle-launcher-4.4.1.jar`, immediate lib and lib/plugins JARs. JAR links may stay in the selecting directory or enter individual matching `/usr/share/java` JARs; subsequent hops stay there. Materialize classpath bytes without exposing that directory. Retain fixed launcher aliases and Java `/usr/bin/java -> /etc/alternatives/java -> /usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64/bin/java`.

Let J = `/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64`, E = `/etc/java-25-openjdk`. Preserve only these exact J-to-E metadata edges:

| J suffix | E suffix |
| --- | --- |
| /lib/jvm.cfg | /jvm-amd64.cfg |
| /conf/security/java.security | /security/java.security |
| /lib/security/blocked.certs | /security/blocked.certs |
| /lib/security/public_suffix_list.dat | /security/public_suffix_list.dat |
| /conf/security/policy/unlimited/default_US_export.policy | /security/policy/unlimited/default_US_export.policy |
| /conf/security/policy/unlimited/default_local.policy | /security/policy/unlimited/default_local.policy |

The last two are the already approved exact public unlimited-policy targets, terminal root-owned 0644 files with trusted ancestors. Preserve their bytes, individual read-only staging, exact-link validation and rejection of extra target hops. No policy directory enumeration or sibling/limited-policy allowance. Preserve algorithm restrictions, built-in-provider validation, include rejection and generated public trust.

All other exclusions remain unchanged: no host settings, caches, homes, credentials, keys, truststores, proxy or logging configuration; never open/import net.properties or logging.properties, even when root-owned. No broad /etc, /usr/share, alternatives, J/conf or installation-tree bind. No host discovery execution, repository-selected inputs or fallback. Preserve broker registry restrictions, direct-socket denial, descriptor closure, fixed helper, canaries, environment and finite limits. No protected prompts/policy, fork files, restore adapters, issue-188 work, native Codex or OCI changes.

Preserve existing bounds: 512 scanned entries per enumerated directory; 1024 selected unique files; 64 MiB/JAR; 512 MiB total; 1 MiB/launcher or textual metadata; 16 MiB/public security data; 4096 pathname bytes; 32 components; 8 link hops; 255-byte matching JAR basenames; 2048 generated entries/aliases and mounts. Keep sorting, deduplication, collision rejection and fail-closed cleanup.

## What we're assuming

The supplied snapshot represents the named preserved candidate and unchanged-source predecessor evidence remains applicable. Cheapest check: coordinator compares exact Git objects and source/test digests with the retained evidence; record its command, revision, outcome and skips. Reuse only evidence whose exercised source and assumptions still match. No new host/performance/probe campaign is planned.

## Open questions

The coordinator must identify which retained source checks remain applicable after the candidate merge. Developer verification below resolves uncovered runtime-input behavior; independent tester review resolves coverage concerns. No failure is established by planning, so no production correction is preselected.

Real Java 25/Maven/Gradle compatibility under unchanged limits and omission of host defaults remains an operator PR-review item to the extent not already covered by the retained host proof. It is not an agent implementation blocker. A demonstrated need for wider inputs, changed budgets or helper/adapter work reopens scope with the maintainer.

## Remaining sequence and exact touchpoints

1. Coordinator binds the named candidate/predecessor and retained evidence; independent review and fresh human plan approval precede developer activity. Operator reconciliation remains separate after approval.
2. Developer reviews existing tests against the manifest and executes only uncovered focused runtime-input checks from TEST_PLAN.md. Reuse applicable unchanged-source evidence; record skips and failures precisely.
3. If a concrete defect or coverage gap is demonstrated, make the smallest correction in existing `internal/sandbox/restore_runtime_linux.go` and/or `internal/sandbox/restore_runtime_linux_test.go`; add a regression that fails on the defective behavior. Modify existing `internal/sandbox/restore_linux_test.go` only for a demonstrated integration assertion gap; `restore_linux.go` only for a demonstrated runtime-flag integration defect. No speculative rewrite. Preserve existing changelog fragment; adjust only if a correction changes its accuracy. No new source files are planned.
4. Independently review source and acceptance coverage, reuse applicable passing developer results, and repeat only for relevant edits, observed failures or unresolved coverage concerns. Resolve concrete findings within these touchpoints or reopen the plan.
5. Coordinator performs final trusted-base required policy once and records claim-bound validation. Satisfy WorkUnit make fmt/make check coverage with coordinator-owned results, avoiding duplicate per-role full suites. Explicit publication and any later reconciliation belong to the operator workflow.

## HANDOFF

- Entry points: `restore_runtime_linux.go:473,556,602,628`; security/traversal symbols `:59,71,163,172,256,266,341,423`; integration `restore_linux.go:43,66`. Change only for a demonstrated defect within the preserved manifest.
- Extend existing `newRuntimeFixture` (`restore_runtime_linux_test.go:30`) and the tests at `:162,218,288,327,381,440,491,518,739,772,819,884` only for demonstrated gaps. Exact focused commands are in TEST_PLAN.md.
- Checked assumptions: files and tests already exist; exact policy targets are in runtimeMetadata; generated classworlds bytes and numeric limits are in current source; generic argv exits before filesystem access. Checked by source inspection, not runtime execution. Commit identity and prior proof applicability require coordinator evidence.
- Reopen for different candidate/predecessor, broader manifest/config import, increased limits, unknown layout, protected-file/helper/adapter/fork changes, weakened adversarial tests or unsupported host requirements. Unavailable host checks alone do not reopen implementation or block fixtures.
- **What this change breaks:** no intentional behavioral/API break. Search found restoreCommand/restoreFlags integration and direct assertions in `restore_linux_test.go:71,311`; preserve signatures and capability behavior. Existing generic-argv and executor assertions (`restore_runtime_linux_test.go:162,491`, `executor_test.go:89`) preserve unchanged. Existing helper/startup tests (`restore_linux_test.go:103,170,419,457,478,495`) preserve unchanged; no startup probe campaign. Restore broker/protocol tests, common RestoreRequest callers, non-Linux launcher, docs/templates and changelog remain unchanged unless the narrow demonstrated correction requires an accurate fragment update. No files are designated new, so no approved-base new-file absence claim is needed.

# ISSUE-311 remaining verification

Applies to candidate `b3e19745c76ef89be1b131edb9a329e953dd6702`, replacing `ca3c72f5020b9378eae53863367be6538c927d95`, with the exact preserved manifest in PLAN.md. Fresh independent review and actual human plan approval are required; reconciliation is a separate subsequent operator action. Planning runs no implementation tests and claims no new pass.

## Evidence reuse and responsibilities

Coordinator first binds candidate/source digests to retained results. Reuse applicable unchanged-source evidence, including the reported passing predecessor actual-host manifest proof; preserve original revision, command, result, environment assumptions and skips in the evidence record. The user reports pure-Go helper installation and Maven package installation complete: do not repeat installation or revive obsolete readiness blockers. Missing retained details are evidence gaps to identify, not authority to invent passes or start new probe/performance campaigns.

Developer owns focused runtime-input verification and minimal demonstrated corrections. Tester independently reviews source and acceptance coverage and reuses applicable passing developer results. Repeat commands only after relevant source changes, observed failures or unresolved coverage concerns. Coordinator owns complete trusted-base policy and claim-bound validation; agent observations are advisory.

## Acceptance 1: deterministic launch and clear pre-execution failures

Use existing TestRestoreRuntimeLayouts, TestRestoreRuntimePublicMetadata, TestRestoreRuntimeExcludedHostDefaults, TestRestoreRuntimeLimits, TestRestoreRuntimeDeduplication, TestRestoreRuntimeAdditionalBudgets and TestRestoreRuntimeBoundary.

Verify both tool-shaped fixtures consume required launcher/JAR/public-security markers, including relative/versioned distribution JAR links, and complete inside the boundary. Assert exact sorted golden destinations, staged byte identity, read-only sources, no /usr/share/java directory exposure and fixed generated m2.conf bytes. Check missing launcher/Java/JAR/bootstrap/plugin layouts, ambiguous Maven bootstrap and both named formerly missing Maven JAR targets separately/together; fail clearly before payload execution, without silently dropping dependencies. Nil/generic argv must work without installed tools.

Both exact unlimited-policy pairs must resolve through the J symlink to its corresponding terminal E target, individually staged read-only with unchanged bytes and counted within unchanged budgets. Existing metadata tables must reject missing J/E, terminal-J substitution, swapped basename, limited-policy/sibling/prefix target, escape-and-return, extra E hop, nonregular target, wrong owner and writable ancestors. Preserve Java-properties continuation/escape/include/provider checks and algorithm bytes. Net/logging omission must be independent of absent, root-owned, credential-bearing, symlink or FIFO host defaults; verify no opens/reads or staging. No synthetic pass implies real-client compatibility.

Focused commands, only when applicable evidence does not cover them:

```bash
go test ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestRestoreRuntime(Layouts|PublicMetadata|ExcludedHostDefaults|Limits|Deduplication|AdditionalBudgets)$' -count=1
go test ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestRestoreRuntimeBoundary$' -count=1
```

Resolver/stager tests run without installed clients, network or namespaces. Boundary launches retain existing capability-based infrastructure skips; record skips, and use retained capable-runner evidence or coordinator/CI coverage for actual launches. Payload or arbitrary startup failures must fail, not acquire new skip classifications.

## Acceptance 2: adversarial isolation and regressions

Use existing TestRestoreRuntimeRejectsUnsafeInputs, TestRestoreRuntimeSnapshot, TestRestoreRuntimePolicyConcurrentChanges, TestRestoreRuntimeBoundaryIntegrity, TestToolExecutorRejectsRestoreRuntimeWidening and boundary fixtures. Review per-hop typed edges, pinned descriptors, permissions, bounded reads, snapshot identity/revalidation, cleanup and deterministic race hooks. Reject homes/source/temp/cache/credentials/settings/key targets through every unsupported link edge, including escape-and-return. Both policy pairs need J-link/E-file/ancestor replacement and mutation coverage; successful snapshots must remain unchanged after host replacement.

Verify denied source/runtime/alias writes, cache escape, host credentials and descriptor reads, direct IPv4/IPv6/loopback/metadata sockets and unapproved broker requests, while approved registry fixture transfer remains functional. Retain namespaces, capabilities, cleared environment, helper protocol, trust, finite limits and fail-closed canaries. Verify ordinary ToolExecutor receives no added runtime mount or selection authority. Do not remove or weaken adversarial tests.

```bash
go test ./internal/sandbox -run '^Test(RestoreRuntime(RejectsUnsafeInputs|Snapshot|PolicyConcurrentChanges|BoundaryIntegrity)|ToolExecutorRejectsRestoreRuntimeWidening)$' -count=1
go test ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestRestoreLinux(Flags|Boundary|FailureCleanup|CapabilityMissingBinary|SourceSpecialFile)$' -count=1
```

Reuse applicable restore/broker/protocol and ordinary-executor boundary results. If a concrete integration/coverage concern requires them, available targeted commands are:

```bash
go test ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestRestore' -count=1
SWARM_TEST_EXECUTOR=1 go test ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestToolExecutorBoundary$' -count=1
```

These broader commands are conditional, not another per-role campaign. Any correction requires a failing-before/passing-after regression and relevant focused rerun. For changed Go files, run gofmt on exactly those files and `go vet ./internal/sandbox`; run focused race checks only for relevant concurrent changes or an unresolved race concern. Record test selection so zero matched tests cannot masquerade as coverage.

## Independent tester review

Independently inspect candidate changes and tests against both acceptance criteria and all preserved exclusions. Verify retained evidence applicability, exact two public-policy edges, no host-default reads, trusted ownership and per-hop checks, unchanged budgets/canaries/broker, and ordinary-executor separation. Inspect boundary assertions and infrastructure skips, including integrity checks that detect payload edits. Reuse passing applicable developer results and document any uncovered concern before selectively repeating a command. No full-suite repetition by default and no self-review substitution for the human gate.

## Coordinator reference policy and completion

Load authoritative required-checks/protected paths from approved base, not candidate policy. After roles finish, run the complete trusted-base required policy once on the final candidate and record fenced validation. WorkUnit acceptance explicitly includes make fmt/make check: coordinator owns their final coverage, including formatting, vet/static analysis, race suite and changelog validation; reuse overlapping final-candidate results where policy permits, without omitting required checks. Agents do not execute the compiled policy as a checklist or request coordinator credentials. Confirm only approved implementation touchpoints changed and protected files/adapters/fork/issue-188 scope stayed untouched.

## Operator PR-review checklist (outside agent implementation gating)

- [ ] Attach available predecessor actual-host manifest proof and identify unchanged candidate source to which it applies; retain exact public-policy target ownership/modes and exclusion evidence. No new host manifest/performance/probe campaign is requested.
- [ ] Record supplied completed pure-Go helper and Maven package installation readiness without repeating installation.
- [ ] Reuse existing applicable installed Maven/Gradle/Java startup/dependency evidence under the same restore boundary. Any outstanding installed-client compatibility, Java-default omission or unchanged-resource-limit check remains a PR review item for operator disposition, never a synthetic-fixture implementation prerequisite. Keep host settings/caches/keys/truststores/proxy/logging excluded and never execute repository build code on the host.
- [ ] Record fresh human approval bound to these artifacts before the separate explicit reconciliation action. Neither this checklist nor historical approval supplies that approval or performs reconciliation.
